newsitem.title: INDIA: India, Russia pledge to strengthen trade ties.
newsitem.headline: India, Russia pledge to strengthen trade ties.

text.p: Russia and India have pledged to strengthen cooperation in metallurgical and power sectors and boost trade, officials from both sides said on Wednesday.

A joint statement released at the end of Russian Deputy Prime Minister Oleg Davydov's five day visit said both sides agreed to speed up measures to construct a 2,000-megawatt nuclear power project in southern India.
Davydov on Monday told reporters Russia and India were nearing agreement on the construction of the power project in Kudankulam town in Tamil Nadu state.
The project was first proposed in 1988 during a visit to India by former Soviet president Mikhail Gorbachev but languished following the breakup of the Soviet Union.

The joint statement said India and Russia had shown satisfaction over the outcome of the recent talks to finalise and sign inter-governmental agreements on avoidance of double taxation and customs cooperation.
"The sides noted the wide scope for closer cooperation in the power and metallurgy sectors," the statement said.
Officials of the two sides reaffirmed the need to widen scope of bilateral trade, especially supply of machinery and high technology items, it said.
Davydov during his visit held talks with Prime Minister H. D. Deve Gowda, Foreign Minister I.K. Gujral and Defence and Finance ministers.
India and Russia have expressed satisfaction over a 54 percent growth in trade turnover in 1995/96 (April-March) over the previous fiscal year.
Trade between the former Soviet Union and its Cold War ally India stood at $5.5 billion in 1990, just before the end of the Soviet Union.
But trade flows, undermined by upheaval in Russia, dried up to a mere $1.1 billion in 1993.
